title: Monday at the service desk
instructions:
## You run the university service desk

Five tickets arrive before 9 a.m. Classify each (incident, service request, problem or change), prioritise by impact and urgency, and decide what to escalate. The SLA table is in the evidence.

nodes.title: Ticket 1
nodes.text: "The student portal is down for everyone; results day is today."

evidence.title: Priority matrix and SLA
evidence.text: Priority = impact × urgency. P1 (whole organisation, now): respond 15 min, resolve 2 h, major incident process. P2 (department): 1 h / 8 h. P3 (one user, work possible): 4 h / 2 days. P4 (request): 1 day / 5 days.

choices.text: Incident, P1, start the major incident process

choices.feedback: Nothing was requested; a service is broken.
A change is planned; this is an outage.

nodes.title: Ticket 2
nodes.text: "Please create an email account for the new lecturer starting next week."

choices.text: Service request, P4, fulfil through the standard process
choices.feedback: Correct. A standard, pre-approved request, not a failure.
A problem is the cause of incidents; this is routine work.

nodes.title: Ticket 3
nodes.text: "The library printer jams every day this month; we fix it each time but it keeps coming back."

choices.text: Open a problem record to find the root cause, alongside the recurring incidents
choices.feedback: Correct. Repeated incidents with the same cause are what problem management exists for.
That is what has been happening all month.

choices.text: A change request to buy a new printer
choices.feedback: Maybe later; first find out why it jams.

nodes.title: Ticket 4
nodes.text: "One lecturer cannot open her email on her laptop; she can use the webmail."

choices.feedback: Correct. One user, with a workaround available.
One user with a workaround is not organisation-wide.
Something that worked has stopped working.

nodes.title: Ticket 5
nodes.text: "We want to upgrade the finance system to the new version this weekend."

choices.text: Change request: assess risk, schedule, get approval, plan a rollback
choices.feedback: Correct. Planned modifications go through change management.
Unassessed changes cause most P1 incidents.

nodes.title: Queue triaged
nodes.text: One major incident, one request, one problem record, one P3 incident and one change for the advisory board. The desk's value is this sorting, done consistently.

hints: Incident = unplanned interruption; request = standard ask; problem = root cause of incidents; change = planned modification.
Priority combines how many are affected with how soon it matters.

checks.label: At least four of the five decisions are right
checks.message: Fewer than four of the five were right. Read the feedback and run the case again.

realityNote: ITIL 4 defines these practices; tools such as ServiceNow, Jira Service Management and GLPI encode the same categories and SLA timers.
